stem: I am diploblastic & acoelomate. Which phylum do I belong to?
My body is radially symmetrical. Water vascular system is present in my body. I am referred as fish though I am not. What is my name?
note: The chapter body never uses the term 'water vascular system' - a text scan of all 16 pages finds it ONLY inside this question. The nearest related statement the chapter makes is that echinoderms 'perform locomotion with the help of tube-feet'. Without that outside term, the chapter's own text makes Jelly fish an equally good fit for the other two clues (Cnidaria is 'radially symmetrical' and Aurelia is printed as 'Jelly fish'). The solution says so.

stem: I live in your small intestine. Pseudocoelom is present in my thread like body. In which phylum will you include me?
Though I am multicellular, there are no tissues in my body. What is the name of my phylum?

Write the characters of each of the following animals with the help of classification chart.

Bath sponge, grasshopper, rohu, penguin, frog, lizard, elephant, jellyfish.
note: Of the eight animals named, seven are printed somewhere in the chapter's own example lists (Bath sponge = Euspongia under Porifera; rohu under Pisces; penguin under Aves; frog under Amphibia; lizard under Reptilia; elephant under Mammalia; Jelly fish = Aurelia under Cnidaria). GRASSHOPPER is NOT printed anywhere in the chapter - the Arthropoda example list is 'Crab, spider, scorpion, millipede, centipede, cockroach, butterfly, honey bee, etc.' The solution says so and places it on the chapter's stated Arthropoda characters rather than on an example.

note: FIGURE-DEPENDENT AND UNANSWERABLE FROM THE STEM. The book prints four unlabelled drawings of animals beside this one-line instruction and nothing else; the entire content of the question is in those drawings. They are not reproduced here and attach-images.ts was deliberately not run. The stored solution states this plainly and points at the chapter's own labelled figures rather than naming the four organisms, which would be inventing the figure's contents.
